headline: Brent just hit a fresh $91 cycle high on renewed US-Iran tension, and PSX rallied over 2,000 points intraday on mediation hopes only to give almost all of it back by the close — the desk stays risk-off into results season and the July 27 rate decision.
summary: Pakistan's market is caught between an oil shock and a shaky rally: Brent just hit a fresh cycle high near $91 on US-Iran tension, while global stocks and the VIX have actually calmed down — so it's PSX's own oil-driven channel (import bill, reserves, the rupee) doing the damage, not global panic. SBP reserves fell to $17.2bn and the current account flipped to a small deficit, with a rate hold at 11.5% almost certain on July 27. The index keeps rallying intraday on mediation headlines then giving it back into the close — a pattern that argues for caution. The desk favours banks and E&P over energy-cost-exposed sectors.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: A high policy rate (11.5%, hold widely expected July 27) keeps bank margins wide, and the desk's fundamental screen backs it up — UBL, HBL, BAFL, NBP, BOP and BAHL all rate 'attractive' on cheap P/Es and well-covered double-digit dividend yields.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Brent's fresh cycle high (~$91, +17% over the month) is a direct tailwind for OGDC, PPL, MARI and POL; POL screens outright cheap and well-covered (7.15x P/E, 11% yield), though OGDC/PPL/MARI already price in more of the good news (fair valuations, not cheap).

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand names with little direct oil-import exposure; ENGROH rates 'attractive' (cheap P/E, healthy margin) while FFC and EFERT are 'mixed' with high but covered payout ratios ahead of FFC's July 29 results.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: PSO's P/E looks cheap on paper but net margin is a wafer-thin 1% — no cushion if the current-account deficit and the new daily fuel-price mechanism keep squeezing distributor economics.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs and an inflation-squeezed consumer remain the macro story; HCAR screens 'caution' on thin margins — INDU is the fundamental exception, but the sector overall still faces the same import-cost headwind.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-cost sensitive names (LUCK, DGKC, FCCL, MLCF, CHCC, BWCL) mostly screen 'mixed' with healthy margins but small dividends; a $91 Brent print raises the input-cost bar the sector has to clear.

sectors.name: Textiles / exporters
sectors.why: June exports fell 16.7% YoY and FY26 exports basically stagnated at $17.9bn; margins across NML, ILP and KTML screen thin-to-fair on the fundamental scan, consistent with the weak print.

watchlist.angle: Today's strongest technical signal on the desk: a 'Volume leads price' (OBV divergence) trigger just fired, and on BML's own history that pattern has won 97% of 89 trades (+5.1% net/trade, still 83% out-of-sample) — rare backtest strength. Fundamentals back it up: 'attractive' rating, a cheap 6.6x P/E and a strong 32% net margin, and it sits in Commercial Banks, the desk's favoured sector into the high-rate environment.
watchlist.risk: No dividend and thinner liquidity than the big-four banks — a broad risk-off reversal (today's session gave back most of a 2,000-point intraday rally) could puncture the signal before the 15-session hold plays out.

watchlist.angle: UBL screens 'attractive' — a fair 8.31x P/E, a strong 30% net margin, and a 6.78% dividend yield covered at a 56% payout — and it reports results on July 22 (scraped estimate, unconfirmed), a real near-term catalyst. It also sits in the desk's own top-10 most-predictable names.
watchlist.risk: The July 22 date is an unconfirmed scraped estimate, not a primary-source filing yet — and a results miss into a risk-off tape (Commercial Banks already cut nearly 700 index points in the last current-account-deficit sell-off) could hit hard.

watchlist.angle: A Donchian-55 breakout ('turtle' style) just triggered — historically a 62% hit rate over 13 trades and +3.6% net expectancy, still profitable out-of-sample (75%) — the desk's highest-confidence breakout signal today.
watchlist.risk: The fundamental screen rates TPLT 'caution': it's currently loss-making with no dividend cushion. This is a technical-only setup — if the breakout fails, there's no earnings support underneath it.

watchlist.angle: Pakistan Oilfields is a direct beneficiary of Brent's push to a fresh ~$91 cycle high, and unlike its E&P peers it actually screens 'attractive' on fundamentals — a cheap 7.15x P/E, a strong 48% net margin, and an 11% dividend yield covered at an 80% payout.
watchlist.risk: The same oil story that helps POL's earnings also feeds Pakistan's import bill and reserve drawdown — if Brent reverses on a genuine ceasefire, the tailwind (and the stock's premium) fades fast.

watchlist.angle: Dolmen City REIT tops the desk's own predictability ranking (score 75.7, the highest on the list) and has a confirmed book closure July 25-27 for a 6.6% final dividend (Rs0.66/share, ex-date July 24) — a real, dated, already-confirmed catalyst.
watchlist.risk: The dividend-safety flag reads 'stretched' — DCR is paying out 106% of earnings, more than it currently earns — and REIT units often drift down by roughly the dividend amount right after the ex-date.

catalysts.event: DCR book closure begins (confirmed, 6.6% final dividend, Rs0.66/share)
SBP MPC — first FY27 rate decision; hold at 11.5% widely expected (97% per Topline Securities survey)
FFL, JDWS, JSML, TBL results (scraped estimates, unconfirmed); LOTCHEM book closure begins (confirmed, 15% dividend)

risks: Brent crude just printed a fresh cycle high near $91 (+17% over the past month) on escalating US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz tension — every extra dollar widens Pakistan's import bill and leans on reserves, PKR and inflation, the actual channel hurting PSX right now even though global equities and the VIX have calmed.

SBP reserves fell $1.245bn (-6.7% WoW) to $17.226bn in the week ended July 10, and the FY26 current account flipped to a $139mn deficit (from a $1.84bn FY25 surplus) with June alone posting a $649mn deficit — a genuine external-account deterioration, not just a headline scare.

The tape itself is fragile: KSE-100 has rallied over 2,000 points intraday twice this week (Jul 20, Jul 21) only to give almost all of it back by the close — sentiment is reversing on headlines faster than fundamentals are changing, right into both results season and the July 27 MPC.
disclaimer: Research, not advice. The desk generates signals; it does not place orders. Losses are expected.
